newsitem.title: GERMANY: German 97 GDP growth of 2.5 pct feasible - banks.
newsitem.headline: German 97 GDP growth of 2.5 pct feasible - banks.

text.p: The German government's forecast of 2.5 percent economic growth in 1997 is attainable but will not be achieved automatically and will require major efforts by economic policymakers, the Federal Association of German Banks said on Tuesday.
In a statement, the association said one important pillar of the projection was an expected five percent rise in capital equipment spending.

"Such an increase lags behind the momentum seen in previous comparable economic cycles but in view of the fundamental structural problems of the German economy it will require special efforts on the part of economic policymakers," the group said.

Fiscal policy faced a particular challenge, the association said, adding that a question mark must be attached to the government's forecast that the budget deficit will be 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) this year -- just below the three percent limit set by the Maastricht Treaty.
All potential for saving must be used at the national, regional and municipal levels of government as well as in the social insurance system, the group said.
